Addressed by #40869. Missing-provider selection is now serialized behind a process-wide semaphore and rechecked after lock acquisition, so concurrent searches share one provider-selection form and then resume their searches outside the lock. A one-minute bound prevents an abandoned selection from poisoning later attempts. The focused five-way concurrency regression verifies exactly one form is created, and the OpenCode Drive check confirms one answer completes all five searches. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Hi, I cloned opencode and used my opencode go subscription with GLM 5.2 (for planning) and deepseek v4 flash (for coding/debugging). I now have local opencode working properly. I unfortunately don't have enough time to go to do a PR and go to official review. I let everybody with a maximum information so that any motivated contributor could transform that. The problem is more subtile: - Most models actually works. Nvidia platform is not really reliable in response time (as an example, deepseek v4 pro sometimes just don't work). - Deepseek is not working out of the box with opencode because opencode doesn't This is the full explanation (generated by glm) + patch I used locally: > ### Root cause > > NVIDIA NIM's DeepSeek v4 reasoning models (`deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro`) **hang indefinitely** when called through opencode because NIM requires `chat_template_kwargs: { enable_thinking: true, thinking: true }` at the request body root to stream `reasoning_content`. Without it, the request never returns — NIM silently stalls rather than erroring. > > opencode routes NVIDIA through `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, which emits the generic `reasoningEffort` field for reasoning models. NIM's DeepSeek v4 endpoint ignores that field and hangs. > > An additional wrinkle: opencode's title/summary generation path (`smallOptions()`) picks the **first** reasoning variant (`none`), which would set `enable_thinking: false` — and NIM hangs on `enable_thinking: false` too. So even after injecting `chat_template_kwargs` on the main request, the title-generation request alone could hang the whole session. > > ### What the patch does > > Scoped to `nvidia` + `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` + model ids containing `deepseek-v4`: > - **`options()`** — injects `chat_template_kwargs: { thinking: true, enable_thinking: true }` as a default-on baseline. > - **`smallOptions()`** — same, so the title/summary path doesn't disable thinking. > - **`reasoningEffort()`** — translates effort variants to the kwarg shape (all efforts keep thinking on, since NIM hangs when `enable_thinking: false`). > > The MiniMax-M3 special-case (pre-existing) and the generic `reasoningEffort` path for other NVIDIA reasoning models are left untouched. > > ### What was tested > > **Verified working through opencode** (`opencode run -m "Reply with exactly: ok"` → `ok`, exit 0): > - ✅ `nvidia/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash` (was hanging, now works) > - ✅ `nvidia/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro` (was hanging, now works — NIM's pro serving is intermittently slow/flaky, but works when NIM is up) > - ✅ `nvidia/mistralai/mistral-medium-3.5-128b` (was already working via generic `reasoningEffort`; confirmed not regressed — note: NIM **rejects** `chat_template_kwargs` for Mistral with 400 "chat_template is not supported for Mistral tokenizers", so the fix is deliberately scoped to DeepSeek v4 only) > - ✅ `nvidia/minimaxai/minimax-m3` (was already working via pre-existing `chat_template_kwargs: { thinking_mode }` handling; unchanged) > - ✅ `nvidia/poolside/laguna-xs-2.1` (reasoning model, works via generic path, no `chat_template_kwargs` needed) > - ✅ `nvidia/z-ai/glm-5.2` (reasoning toggle model, works via generic path) > > **Not working (NIM-side issue, not fixable from opencode):** > - ❌ `nvidia/google/gemma-4-31b-it` — hangs on **every** request shape, including a plain `curl` with no tools, no system message, no `chat_template_kwargs`. The model id is valid (returned by `/v1/models`) but never responds. NVIDIA's own developer forum confirms: ["Gemma 4 31b has a bug; it is completely unusable, both the API and the playground."](https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/gemma-4-31b-internal-server-error/377468) This is an NVIDIA-side deployment issue, independent of this patch. > > **Why the fix is scoped to DeepSeek v4 and not all N

I think the main issue is that you have to install the plugin separately for every harness, which means it ends up duplicated across multiple places in your system. That's not an approach I really like.

What I do instead is keep a global `.agents/skills` directory and a `.agents/AGENTS.md` file, then use symlinks so every harness shares the same source of truth. Ideally, plugins would work the same way: you'd install them once at the system level, and every harness would automatically discover and use them without any additional setup.

Adding two data points from a downstream consumer (Hermes Agent), since this
directly affects every strict SSE client that refuses to fabricate terminal
markers:

**1. The defect is model-specific, not path-wide.** Same tiny probe
(`Reply with exactly: X`), same `POST /zen/go/v1/chat/completions` endpoint,
streaming + non-streaming:

| Model | finish_reason (non-stream) | Terminal [DONE]/finish_reason (stream) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-5.6-luna | `null` | missing — final chunk `{"choices":[],"cost":"0"}` | 🔴 broken |
| kimi-k3 | `null` | missing — same shape | 🔴 broken |
| kimi-k2.7-code | `stop` | present + `[DONE]` | 🟢 ok |
| glm-5.2 | `stop` | present + `[DONE]` | 🟢 ok |
| deepseek-v4-flash | `stop` | present + `[DONE]` | 🟢 ok |
| deepseek-v4-pro | `stop` | present + `[DONE]` | 🟢 ok |
| minimax-m3 | `stop` | present + `[DONE]` | 🟢 ok |

So the missing termination is confined to the 5.6-family (and kimi-k3) on
the chat/completions compatibility path, not a global behavior of that
endpoint.

**2. Downstream impact + current workaround.** Hermes deliberately refuses
to stamp `finish_reason="stop"` on streams that end without one (it guards a
real truncation class — see NousResearch/hermes-agent#32086), so every luna /
kimi-k3 response was treated as a mid-stream drop and every turn failed with
"Response remained truncated after 4 continuation attempts". The fallback
chain never engaged because the transport succeeds (HTTP 200, full content
delivered) — the defect is semantic, not a connection error.

Until this is fixed upstream, affected clients can either avoid the model on
this path (use `/zen/go/v1/responses` where the termination is correct, or
route to another model) or apply a narrow model-scoped bypass. We published
a small patch script for the Hermes-side guard as a stopgap:
https://gist.github.com/jcmpgit/60087ac45da47c58ffe654781bada8fc

Happy to run any additional probes if it helps isolate where the terminal
marker is being dropped on the gateway side.

**Workaround available (verified working 2026-08-07).**

Confirmed root cause matches #39881: the OpenCode Go chat/completions path never sends a terminal `finish_reason` / `[DONE]` for `gpt-5.6-luna` (and `kimi-k3`), while other models on the same endpoint return `finish_reason:"stop"` + `[DONE]`. Hermes deliberately refuses to fabricate a terminal marker on a text-only stream (guards a real truncation class — NousResearch/hermes-agent#32086), so the response is treated as a mid-stream drop and every turn fails with "Response remained truncated after 4 continuation attempts".

Since this is an upstream endpoint defect, we shipped a narrow, model-scoped client-side workaround rather than waiting: a patch script that lets Hermes treat luna streams as complete (text IS fully delivered — only the terminal marker is missing):

https://gist.github.com/jcmpgit/60087ac45da47c58ffe654781bada8fc

- Applies one boolean clause to the Hermes drop-guard, scoped to `gpt-5.6-luna` only (extendable to `kimi-k3`)
- Backs up the target file before patching; `revert` restores it
- Requires restarting the Hermes gateway/dashboard service after apply
- Note: trade-off is a genuine truncation of the bypassed model would be silently accepted as complete — acceptable as a stopgap

For maintainers: the fix belongs upstream — either emit `finish_reason:"stop"` / `[DONE]` on the chat/completions path for these models, or route luna to the `/zen/go/v1/responses` path where termination is already correct (see #39881). Happy to run additional probes if useful.

blak0p's layer 1 is the part I have numbers for. I run that manifest shape in production and "~50 tokens" is optimistic once signatures are in it: 7 servers and 290 tools come to 2.4 kB, call it 600 tokens, against 295 kB for the full schemas.

The split is what makes layer 1 cheap: of those 295 kB, 273 kB is JSON Schema and only 22 kB is names and descriptions. Keeping per-tool names for small servers and collapsing a 189-tool one to a count costs very little over server-level lines.

What layer 2 won't fix: out of context, out of mind. Over two days I logged 21 calls to a code-index server against 270 greps into the repos it had indexed. The manifest line was in the prompt the whole time. Runtime resolution makes the call cheap once the agent decides to make it, not more likely that it decides.

Numbers and method, my own tool so discount accordingly: https://github.com/TheFox666/mduct#the-context-bill-is-a-side-effect-of-the-pipe

For future reference/others, this is what I did.

First, extracted the (useful) code from the docker file of the mentioned repository.

```bash
export PROVIDER_DIR=/usr/local/provider

bun install "github:ophiosdev/azure-foundry-provider"
cd node_modules/azure-foundry-provider
bun build --outdir=dist src/index.ts
mv dist "${PROVIDER_DIR}/azure-foundry-provider"
```

Second, in my `opencode.json` file added this provider:

```jsonc
  "provider": {
    // all the other stuff...
    "azure-foundry": {
      "name": "Azure Foundry",
      "npm": "file:///usr/local/provider/azure-foundry-provider/index.js",
      "models": {
        "gpt-5.3-codex": {
          "id": "gpt-5.3-codex",
          "name": "Mine - gpt-5.3-codex"
        }
      },
      "options": {
        "apiKey": "[my-api-key]",
        "endpoint": "https://[ai-foundry-resource].cognitiveservices.azure.com/openai/responses?api-version=2025-04-01-preview",
        "apiMode": "responses",
        "useCompletionUrls": false
      }
    }

Agreed overlap (fine to deduplicate):

New root causes this issue adds that are not tracked elsewhere:
1. **The published VSIX ships WITHOUT `dist/extension.js` entirely.** This is the most severe finding: `package.json` declares `"main": "./dist/extension.js"`, but the installed package contains no `dist/` directory at all (and the `.vsixmanifest` assets list only `package.json`, `readme.md`, `icon.png`). An extension whose main module is absent cannot activate regardless of the ENOENT or view-type fixes above. This packaging defect is worth tracking as its own item.
2. **The webview view is missing `"type": "webview"`** (declared as a plain tree view), so `WebviewViewProvider` is never invoked even after activation succeeds.
3. **Missing `onView:opencode-v2.panel` activation event** for the activity-bar view.
4. **Blocking synchronous calls during activation** (e.g. `execSync("npm root -g")`, synchronous PATH scanning) caused the extension host to become unresponsive - a separate failure mode from the ENOENT issue.

Because of #1, #3, and #4 above, I'd suggest keeping this open as a packaging + view-registration fix, while deferring the Windows spawn behavior to #38376. Happy to consolidate or cross-link the comments as the maintainers prefer.

## Follow-up: component-level reproduction narrows the cause

I ran a controlled follow-up using an isolated server, the same installed source revision, and the same large repository. This changes one part of the original diagnosis: `Fff.create()` is not the reproduced primary blocker.

- Direct `Fff.create()` calls completed in 5–39 ms.
- Disabling FFF did not improve cold Location acquisition.
- No individual Location service accounted for the complete unavailable interval.

The repeatable boundary is aggregate Location acquisition on the server's main event loop, with MCP startup materially amplifying it.

### Controlled results

| Configuration | Cold Location | Worst health during startup | Worst health in following 8s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All MCPs enabled | 625 ms | 375 ms | 406 ms |
| All MCPs disabled | 234 ms | 97 ms | 123 ms |
| Chrome DevTools only | 248 ms | 36 ms | 124 ms |
| Context7 only | 287 ms | 36 ms | 156 ms |
| Railway only | 378 ms | 36 ms | 205 ms |
| FFF disabled, all MCPs enabled | 851 ms | 271 ms | 217 ms |

In the most detailed run, the individually measured components were modest: Project resolution 133 ms, Config 90 ms, MCP layer acquisition 127 ms, FileSystem/Search 71 ms, and `Fff.create()` 5 ms. Despite that, a timer scheduled for 20 ms was delayed by 521 ms and an external health request took 505 ms. This points to aggregate event-loop starvation rather than one consistently slow node.

### MCP lifecycle finding

MCP state is Location-scoped. The live service retained four Locations and correspondingly had four Chrome DevTools MCP roots and four Railway MCP roots. Disabling the MCP group substantially reduced cold-start and post-start health latency.

No individual MCP reproduced the severe historical stall by itself. The evidence supports a cumulative per-Location multiplier, not one defective MCP server.

### Evidence boundary

This follow-up establishes that Location acquisition can delay unrelated HTTP handling on the shared event loop, eager per-Location MCP startup amplifies that delay, and FFF is not the reproduced primary cause.

It does **not** identify the callback responsible for the historical 53-second event, prove that one MCP caused it, or establish that every MCP can safely be shared globally.

The strongest candidate improvements are:

1. Keep health/lifecycle handling responsive independently of Location acquisition.
2. Make MCP startup lazy or incrementally warmed.
3. Bound concurrent MCP initialization.
4. Share MCP processes where configuration, credentials, and isolation permit it.
5. Dispose inactive Location-scoped resources more aggressively.
6. Add permanent per-node acquisition and event-loop-delay telemetry.

Related lifecycle/process reports: #37795 and #31554.

A controlled follow-up to #37794 reproduced the upstream condition for this failure: aggregate Location acquisition delayed authenticated health responses, with eager per-Location MCP startup acting as a cumulative amplifier.

The two-second discovery timeout therefore remains capable of treating a live incumbent as unavailable. I added the measurements and evidence boundary to #37794 so the investigation stays consolidated there: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/37794#issuecomment-5215749616
